advances: Mass and cap representation for a marked true centroid; it supplies no cap lower bound.

proof:
The centroid is a positive weighted average of the lifted fiber centroids. Their weights show $0\in\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}P$, and their Minkowski average with the same weights lies in $K_0$ and has positive $d$-volume. Every integer point in $\operatorname{conv}P$ is similarly the base of a positive-volume Minkowski average, so belongs to $P$. Containment in $C$ and inclusion of its positive fibers now give the asserted fiber equality. The affine hull of $C_*$ is $\operatorname{span}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$, since every lifted positive fiber spans its continuous direction space. A nonzero supporting linear functional at $0$ in this space would be nonnegative on $C_*$ and have zero mixed integral. It would vanish on each positive fiber by continuity and full relative support of fiber volume, contradicting the affine hull.

Each nonzero integer vector has a unique expression $kp$ with $k>0$ the gcd of its coordinates and $p$ signed primitive. For $1\le i\le k$, convexity with the actual origin gives $(i/k)K_{kp}\subseteq K_{ip}$, which proves no gaps and nesting. Substituting $x=ks$ has Jacobian $k^d$ and contributes one further $k$ to each first moment. It converts the cap margin at $(kp,ks)$ into $k(a\cdot p+u\cdot s)$, giving all four identities, including the full boundary contribution when $u=0$ and $a\cdot p=0$. The gauge is finite and positive off zero, and $k(p,s)\in C_*$ holds exactly when $k\rho(p,s)\le1$. Each such integer $k$ belongs to the same positive ray family by the proven equality of nonempty integer fibers. This yields the exact floor, including on possible plateaus.

statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex, $d\ge1$, with positive summed integer-fiber volume $M$ and true mixed centroid of integer base. Translate by this centroid, let $K_z$ be the translated fibers, set $P=\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:|K_z|_d>0\}$, and let $C_*=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$. Its nonempty integer fibers are exactly the $K_z$ for $z\in P$, $0\in P$, and $0$ is interior to $C_*$ in $\operatorname{span}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. On each signed primitive ray $p$ meeting $P\setminus\{0\}$ the positive indices are $kp$, $1\le k\le N_p$, and the bodies $Q_{p,k}=k^{-1}K_{kp}$ decrease with $k$. Put $f_p(s)=\sum_{k=1}^{N_p}k^d\mathbf 1_{Q_{p,k}}(s)$ and $g_p(s)=\sum_{k=1}^{N_p}k^{d+1}\mathbf 1_{Q_{p,k}}(s)$. Then
$$
M=|K_0|_d+\sum_p\int f_p,\qquad \sum_p p\int g_p=0,\qquad
\int_{K_0}x\,dx+\sum_p\int s\,g_p(s)\,ds=0.
$$
The mixed mass of every closed halfspace $a\cdot z+u\cdot x\ge0$ equals $|K_0\cap\{u\cdot x\ge0\}|_d+\sum_p\int_{\{a\cdot p+u\cdot s\ge0\}} f_p(s)\,ds$. If $\rho$ is the gauge of $C_*$ on its relative space, the count of contributing indices at $s$ is $\lfloor1/\rho(p,s)\rfloor$, including equality at integer radii.
title: Primitive-ray formulas at the true mixed centroid
